payload.problem_addressed: Self-evolving LLM agents that unconditionally admit distilled skills into their runtime context suffer a non-monotone capability trajectory: performance peaks then collapses as contaminated skills accumulate and propagate through later distillation.
payload.method_summary: Verifier-as-Gatekeeper (VaG): a pre-commit, progressive trust hierarchy (Cold->Warm->Hot) gating each newly distilled skill before it can enter the agent's runtime context. Gate 1 (individual harmlessness) requires a skill to pass three heterogeneous critics -- a deterministic schema/structural-validity check, a single-skill A-B replay on held-out tasks, and one LLM semantic-consistency review -- combined by conjunction. Gate 2 (combinatorial safety) performs marginal-gain greedy subset selection on the Warm pool against measured joint held-out performance, promoting a skill to Hot only if it strictly improves the set.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper identifies and formalizes a 'capability-contamination tipping point' in self-evolving LLM agents, showing skill accumulation is non-monotone and that contamination is structurally irreversible because later skills are distilled conditioned on earlier (possibly defective) ones, so post-hoc rollback of a source skill cannot undo the flawed reasoning inherited by its descendants. It proposes VaG, a pre-commit gating mechanism combining three complementary per-skill critics with marginal-gain greedy subset selection, and demonstrates on Terminal-Bench 2 that VaG improves monotonically across five evolution rounds (reaching 72% pass@1 with a 5x smaller pool) versus ungated evolution's peak-then-collapse pattern, with the gated pool transferring positively across five backbones and to a second benchmark.
key_architecture_choices: Progressive trust hierarchy with three tiers: Cold (recorded, invisible) -> Warm (individually verified) -> Hot (runtime-injected)

Gate 1 conjunction of three heterogeneous, disjoint-failure-surface critics: SchemaCritic (deterministic structural validity), ExecCritic (single-skill A-B replay requiring R(M+{s}) >= R(M)), AgentCritic (one LLM call for fabrication/contradiction/unsafe-content)
Gate 2 marginal-gain greedy subset selection (not full 2^|W| enumeration) targeting combinatorial contamination that per-skill checks cannot detect
Cheap-first ordering: the two no-LLM-call checks (schema, replay) run before the LLM semantic check to filter most candidates economically
datasets: Terminal-Bench 2 (TB2) -- Event/Holdout/Test splits of hard, verifier-checked CLI tasks
InterCode NL2Bash (200 tasks) for cross-benchmark transfer
metrics: recovery gap (pp recovered by post-hoc rollback vs. full-lineage oracle cleanup)
payload.headline_results: On TB2, ungated evolution peaks at 62% pass@1 (R3, 105 skills) then collapses to 50% (R5, 179 skills); VaG instead rises monotonically to 72% pass@1 at R5 with only 37 skills, a 5x smaller pool, and 22pp above ungated at R5. Source-only post-hoc rollback recovers only 1.7pp of the 12.3pp peak-to-R5 drop; even oracle full-lineage cleanup recovers only 6.7pp, leaving 5.6pp structurally irrecoverable. The frozen VaG pool transfers with +8 to +16pp lift across five backbones (Hy3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) with no re-evolution, and to InterCode NL2Bash (69.0% vs. Ungated's 65.5% with 5x fewer skills).
claimed_advantages: Monotone improvement across evolution rounds instead of a peak-then-collapse trajectory
Much smaller, cleaner skill pool for equal or better performance (lower per-trial token cost)
Gate 1's two cheapest checks require no LLM calls, so verification cost is small relative to what it prevents
Ablations show the three Gate-1 critics are complementary and mutually non-substitutable (each intercepts a largely disjoint class of harmful skills)
Frozen gated pool generalizes across backbones and to a second, structurally different benchmark without re-evolution
limitations: Removing the marginal-gain gate (Gate 2) still leaves individually-passing skills that conflict in combination, showing per-skill judgment alone is insufficient and Gate 2 evaluation cost scales with Warm-pool size (<=14 joint replays/round in their setting)
Confidence intervals at intermediate rounds overlap (n=50, k=3 rollouts), so the paper leans on trajectory-shape (monotone vs. single-peaked) rather than per-round significance

Results are from a small, controlled setup (TB2 Event-50, one backbone driving distillation) explicitly not compared head-to-head against larger-scale self-evolution systems (ACE, AHE) that differ in backbone/round budget
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The core transferable mechanism is the pre-commit, multi-critic gating pattern applied to our own best-of-N verifier-screened candidate generation and any self-improvement/distillation loop we build around hexgen: (1) the 'irreversibility' argument -- that data/programs generated conditioned on a prior, possibly-flawed pool propagate contamination into later training rounds -- is directly relevant if we ever bootstrap new (B-rep, program) training pairs from the model's own verified outputs (rejection-sampled SFT / self-play flywheel), since a subtly-bad verified program could still bias later generations; this argues for pre-commit filtering of self-generated training data rather than only post-hoc pool cleanup. (2) The heterogeneous, cheap-first, conjunctive critic design (deterministic structural check -> behavioral replay -> expensive semantic/LLM check) is a reusable template for staging our own frozen verifier (compiles -> zero-inverted -> quality bounds -> feature-edge capture) to front-load the cheapest checks. (3) Marginal-gain greedy subset selection for catching combinatorial (not just individual) failure modes could inform how we curate a growing self-play training corpus, since two individually-valid synthesized programs could still be redundant or jointly harmful to training-set diversity/quality.
payload.reviewer_notes: This is an agent-skill-library paper (Terminal-Bench 2 CLI tasks), not CAD/mesh generation -- the bridge to hexgen is purely at the level of the self-improvement/verifier-gating methodology, not the domain. The 'structural validity' critic here (SchemaCritic) is a much weaker notion (frontmatter schema check) than our frozen geometric verifier, so don't over-read the terminology overlap. Worth citing as evidence for why any future self-play/rejection-sampling loop for hexgen should gate admission of new synthetic training examples before they influence subsequent generations, not just filter at generation time.
dependencies_on_other_methods: GRPO/replay infrastructure not required -- gating is a pipeline-stage add-on, not a training-algorithm change

provenance.method_summary: Verifier-as-Gatekeeper (VaG): a progressive trust hierarchy whose three heterogeneous critics—structural validity, behavioral harmlessness, and semantic consistency—filter each skill individually, coupled with a marginal-gain subset selection

payload.problem_addressed: One-shot text-to-CAD decoders cannot use execution outcomes to repair their own predictions: a single invalid parameter or inconsistent operation can prevent execution, and syntactically valid code can still instantiate the wrong geometry, but prior feedback-guided methods treat critique as a fixed, unoptimized heuristic (external reviewer, fixed prompt, or auxiliary reasoning trace) rather than a learned decision.
payload.method_summary: RA-CAD (ReAct Agent for CAD) runs a state-aware Generate-Execute-Critique-Rewrite loop: at each round the agent proposes/rewrites CAD code, a CAD executor runs it and returns validity + diagnostics, and a critique policy conditioned on the post-execution state either accepts the code (terminates) or emits revision guidance that conditions the next rewrite. Training has two stages: CAD Code Bootstrapping (CCB), supervised fine-tuning (teacher forcing, cross-entropy) to learn basic parametric CAD syntax; and Feedback-driven Agent Optimization (FAO), which applies trajectory-level GRPO to the full interaction trajectory (code-generation tokens AND critique tokens together), with a terminal reward combining an F1 score over sketch topological tokens (line/arc/circle) and an exponential-decay reward on Chamfer Distance between instantiated and ground-truth geometry (zero reward if the code fails to execute).
payload.contributions_summary: The paper formulates state-aware text-to-CAD generation as a closed loop with post-execution critique modeled as an explicit, learnable agent-side policy component rather than a fixed prompt or post-hoc reviewer. It introduces trajectory-level Feedback-driven Agent Optimization (FAO) built on CAD Code Bootstrapping (CCB), which assigns terminal CAD-quality rewards (F1 + Chamfer Distance) to the entire Generate-Execute-Critique-Rewrite trajectory and jointly optimizes code generation, critique, and rewriting via GRPO. Experiments on CADFusion and Text2CAD show this closed-loop approach achieves state-of-the-art execution validity and geometric quality versus prior text-to-CAD methods and strong proprietary LLMs used as 8-shot baselines.
key_architecture_choices: ReAct-style state st = (d, c_t, e_t, f_t): design description, current code, execution result, critique
Composite action a_t = (code proposal/rewrite, critique) factorized as two conditional policies pi^{g&r} and pi^{crit}, jointly trained
Two-stage training: CCB (SFT with teacher forcing) to bootstrap valid CAD syntax, then FAO (GRPO) over full trajectories including critique tokens
Terminal-only trajectory reward R = lambda1*R_F1 + lambda2*R_CD, with R_CD = 0 whenever the final code is not executable (hard execution-validity gate baked into the reward)
GRPO with group-relative advantage normalization and clipped surrogate objective, KL-regularized toward a reference policy
Base model: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct with LoRA for CCB; FSDP-distributed FAO via AgentLightning framework
datasets: CADFusion dataset (~20k text-CAD pairs, reparameterized with SkexGen's parameter sequence construction)
Text2CAD dataset (~60k pairs, intermediate-level text descriptions only)
metrics: Average Chamfer Distance (Avg CD) and Median CD between instantiated and ground-truth point clouds
Invalidity Ratio (IR) -- fraction of generated code that fails to execute
Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) between generated and ground-truth parameter distributions
payload.headline_results: On CADFusion, RA-CAD reaches Avg F1 85.30, Avg CD 35.44, IR 6.20 -- improving over CADFusion (83.59 F1, 42.08 CD, 21.98 IR) and Text2CAD (76.05 F1, 41.50 CD, 65.72 IR) baselines. On Text2CAD dataset, RA-CAD gets Avg CD 38.86 and IR 9.44 vs. CADFusion's 49.78/21.85 and Text2CAD's 42.98/71.76. Against proprietary 8-shot LLMs (GPT-4o, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.6-Pro, Qwen3.7-Flash), RA-CAD has the best IR by a large margin (6.20 vs. 54-88 for others on CADFusion) despite comparable or slightly lower F1 on some models. Ablation: removing CCB makes the model unable to generate valid code at all (IR 100); removing FAO/GRPO but keeping the agent loop (CCB+critique, no GRPO) still improves over CCB-only; removing the critique component while keeping GRPO degrades Avg F1 from 85.30->84.93 and IR from 6.20->11.46, showing the learned critique-rewrite mechanism contributes gains beyond the reward optimization itself.
claimed_advantages: Explicitly factorizes and learns post-execution critique as a policy decision rather than treating it as a fixed prompt or external reviewer
Trajectory-level GRPO jointly optimizes code generation, critique, and rewriting instead of optimizing generation alone with feedback as heuristic auxiliary signal
Substantially lower invalidity ratio (execution failure rate) than both prior specialized methods and general-purpose proprietary LLMs used zero/few-shot
Reward directly ties to execution success (R_CD = 0 if non-executable), tightly coupling the learning signal to structural/executable validity
limitations: Ablation shows CCB (SFT bootstrapping) is a hard prerequisite -- without it the model cannot produce valid code at all (100% invalidity), so the method is not usable without a supervised warm start
Reward is defined only on the final trajectory outcome (terminal, not per-step), so critique behavior is optimized only implicitly through credit assignment across the whole trajectory

Paper's own future-work items: no direct visual conditioning, no analysis of per-round convergence behavior, and CAD/domain generalization beyond CADFusion/Text2CAD sketch-extrude representations is untested
Evaluated only on sketch-extrude parametric CAD (line/arc/circle + extrude), not on B-rep or other CAD program families
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: This is a close methodological match to hexgen's structural-validity problem (care area 1) and worth studying closely: (1) the Generate-Execute-Critique-Rewrite loop with an explicit, learned critique policy conditioned on execution feedback is a candidate mechanism for repairing hexgen's own broken best-of-N rollouts -- instead of (or in addition to) discarding candidates that fail the frozen verifier, a trained critique/rewrite step could target-fix them, directly relevant to the 'repair/edit distillation, DAgger-style learning to fix a model's own broken rollouts' line item. (2) The reward design -- hard-zeroing the geometric-fidelity reward whenever the candidate program fails to execute -- mirrors how our own frozen verifier's pass/fail gate could be composed with a continuous quality signal (scaled-Jacobian/aspect-ratio/surface-fidelity) for a GRPO-style trajectory-level RL stage on top of hexgen's current supervised-imitation training. (3) Trajectory-level (not per-step) reward assignment over an interaction that includes both generation and self-critique tokens is a concrete recipe if we want to add an RL fine-tuning stage after hexgen's current SFT-on-inverse-factory-data regime. (4) The ablation isolating the contribution of the critique component (removing it while keeping GRPO degrades performance) is useful evidence that a dedicated repair/critique head, not just outcome-reward RL, is worth the added complexity.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is parametric sketch-extrude CAD code (not B-rep/hex-meshing), and the base model is a general LLM (Llama-3-8B) rather than a small graph-transformer with pointer/copy heads, so architecture details do not transfer directly -- the transferable content is the training-loop pattern (execute -> critique -> rewrite -> trajectory-level RL with an execution-gated reward), not the network design. Baselines are 8-shot-prompted proprietary LLMs, which is a somewhat easy comparison; the more informative comparison for us is the CCB/FAO/Critique ablation in Table 3. Chamfer Distance and F1-over-topological-tokens are the fidelity metrics used; our own verifier's scaled-Jacobian/aspect-ratio/surface-match criteria would need their own reward shaping if adapting this recipe.
dependencies_on_other_methods: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization, from DeepSeekMath)
SkexGen parameter-sequence construction for CAD code representation
AgentLightning framework for distributed agent RL training
CADFusion/Text2CAD datasets and their evaluation protocols

provenance.headline_results: it reduced the Avg CD to 35.44 and IR to 6.20, and for the Text2CAD dataset, it reduced the Avg CD to 38.86 and IR to 9.44
